docker-architecture.title: Docker architecture
docker-architecture.description: The CLI talks to the daemon over an API. The daemon stores images and delegates container execution to containerd, shims and runc.

nodes.label: Docker CLI
nodes.detail: Parses commands and calls the Docker API. It is a client, not the engine.

nodes.label: dockerd
nodes.detail: The long-running daemon that owns Docker objects and serves the API.

nodes.label: containerd
nodes.detail: Prepares snapshots and delegates execution to an OCI runtime.

nodes.label: containerd-shim
nodes.detail: Keeps the container alive if containerd restarts and reports exit status.

nodes.label: Registry
nodes.detail: Stores and distributes image manifests and layer blobs.

nodes.label: Image store
nodes.detail: Local layer store. Shared layers are stored once.

nodes.label: Container process
nodes.detail: An isolated process using the host kernel, constrained by cgroups.

image-layers.title: Image layers and copy-on-write
image-layers.description: Read-only layers are shared between images. A container adds one writable layer on top.

nodes.label: Writable container layer
nodes.detail: Changes at runtime are written here using copy-on-write. It is not part of the image.

nodes.label: Application layer
nodes.detail: Your application and build output.

nodes.label: Dependency layer
nodes.detail: Installed dependencies. Cache this layer independently of source edits.

nodes.label: Runtime layer
nodes.detail: Language runtime and system packages.

nodes.label: Base layer
nodes.detail: The base image filesystem. Pin its version for reproducibility.

nodes.label: Image
nodes.detail: The image is the stack of read-only layers plus config metadata.

container-lifecycle.title: Container lifecycle
container-lifecycle.description: A container is created, runs while PID 1 lives, and remains in the exited state until removed.

nodes.label: Created
nodes.detail: docker create allocates the container without starting it.

nodes.label: Running
nodes.detail: The main process is running. Exec starts extra processes.

nodes.label: Paused
nodes.detail: Processes are frozen but state is preserved.

nodes.label: Restarting
nodes.detail: A restart policy is restarting the container.

nodes.label: Exited
nodes.detail: PID 1 terminated. The writable layer and name remain.

nodes.label: Removed
nodes.detail: docker rm deletes the container and its writable layer.

runtime-stack.title: Runtime stack
runtime-stack.description: Each layer has a narrow responsibility. Runc is short-lived; the shim supervises the process.

nodes.label: docker CLI
nodes.detail: Sends API requests.

nodes.label: dockerd
nodes.detail: Owns Docker objects.

nodes.label: containerd
nodes.detail: Delegates execution.

nodes.label: shim
nodes.detail: Outlives containerd.

nodes.label: runc
nodes.detail: Execs the container process and exits.

nodes.label: container process
nodes.detail: The application process.

delivery-flow.title: Build, ship, run
delivery-flow.description: The same immutable image moves through environments. Configuration is injected at runtime.

nodes.label: Source + Dockerfile
nodes.detail: Code, Dockerfile and .dockerignore define the build.

nodes.label: Build
nodes.detail: Produces an immutable image.

nodes.label: Image
nodes.detail: The artifact that is promoted.

nodes.label: Registry
nodes.detail: Stores and serves the image.

nodes.label: Run
nodes.detail: Containers from the same image in every environment.

nodes.label: Runtime config
nodes.detail: Configuration is injected at runtime, never rebuilt into the image.

network-topology.title: Bridge network topology
network-topology.description: Containers attach to a host bridge. User-defined bridges provide embedded DNS and isolation.

nodes.label: Internet
nodes.detail: Traffic reaches published ports through host NAT.

nodes.label: Host network
nodes.detail: The host routes and NATs container traffic.

nodes.label: docker0 / app-net
nodes.detail: A virtual switch. User-defined bridges provide DNS.

nodes.label: api
nodes.detail: Reachable by name on the network.

nodes.label: db
nodes.detail: Not exposed to the host unless published.

nodes.label: proxy
nodes.detail: Only the proxy publishes 80/443.

compose-architecture.title: Compose project model
compose-architecture.description: A Compose file resolves into a project. Resource names are prefixed with the project name.

nodes.label: compose.yaml
nodes.detail: Declarative model, optionally merged with override files.

nodes.label: Compose CLI
nodes.detail: Resolves variables, validates and calls the Docker API.

nodes.label: Project
nodes.detail: The isolation boundary. Resource names are prefixed.

nodes.label: Services
nodes.detail: Containers with configuration, dependencies and health.

nodes.label: Networks
nodes.detail: Project networks and external networks.

nodes.label: Volumes
nodes.detail: Persistent storage declared by the project.

nodes.label: Secrets / configs
nodes.detail: Files mounted at runtime, not baked into images.

volume-storage.title: Where container data lives
volume-storage.description: The writable layer is disposable. Volumes and bind mounts persist; tmpfs lives in memory.

nodes.label: Container
nodes.detail: Sees mount points as ordinary paths.

nodes.label: Writable layer
nodes.detail: Copied-on-write files. Not persistent.

nodes.label: Named volume
nodes.detail: Lives under the Docker root, survives containers.

nodes.label: Bind mount
nodes.detail: Direct host path. UID/GID and permissions are shared.

nodes.label: tmpfs
nodes.detail: RAM-backed, removed on stop. Good for secrets and scratch space.

nodes.label: Backup
nodes.detail: Back up volumes with a helper container and test restores.

build-process.title: BuildKit build pipeline
build-process.description: The Dockerfile is parsed into a DAG. Independent steps run in parallel and results are content-addressed in the cache.

nodes.label: Build context
nodes.detail: Files sent to the builder. Smaller is faster.

nodes.label: Dockerfile
nodes.detail: Parsed into build operations.

nodes.label: Build DAG
nodes.detail: Independent stages can run concurrently.

nodes.label: Cache store
nodes.detail: Content-addressed layer cache and persistent cache mounts.

nodes.label: Image
nodes.detail: The final stage output.

nodes.label: Registry
nodes.detail: Multi-platform results are pushed as an index.

k8s-architecture.title: Kubernetes architecture
k8s-architecture.description: Everything goes through the API server. The control plane stores and decides; each node runs what it is told.

nodes.label: kubectl
nodes.detail: Talks to the API server over HTTPS. It never touches nodes or pods directly.

nodes.label: kube-apiserver
nodes.detail: The only component that reads and writes cluster state. Authenticates, authorises and validates every request.

nodes.label: etcd
nodes.detail: Consistent key-value store holding every object. Only the API server talks to it.

nodes.label: kube-scheduler
nodes.sub: picks a node for each Pod
nodes.detail: Watches for Pods without a node and assigns one based on resources, affinity and taints.

nodes.label: controller-manager
nodes.detail: Runs controllers (Deployment, ReplicaSet, Node, Job...) that keep actual state equal to desired state.

nodes.label: kubelet
nodes.detail: Runs on each node. Starts the containers of Pods assigned to it and reports their status.

nodes.label: kube-proxy
nodes.detail: Programs the node network rules so Service IPs reach the right Pods.

nodes.label: container runtime
nodes.detail: Pulls images and runs containers on behalf of the kubelet.

k8s-declarative-loop.title: The declarative loop
k8s-declarative-loop.description: You declare the desired state. Controllers keep comparing it with reality and fix the difference, forever.

nodes.label: Manifest
nodes.detail: What you want: image, replicas, ports. You describe the end result, not the steps.

nodes.label: kubectl apply
nodes.detail: Submits the manifest. Re-applying the same file is safe: nothing changes if nothing differs.

nodes.label: Stored object
nodes.detail: spec is what you asked for; status is what the cluster reports back.

nodes.label: Controller
nodes.detail: Watches objects and creates, updates or deletes others until reality matches spec.

nodes.label: Running state
nodes.detail: The actual world. If a Pod dies, the controller notices the drift and replaces it.

k8s-pod-lifecycle.title: Pod lifecycle
k8s-pod-lifecycle.description: A Pod moves through phases. Most problems show up as a Pod stuck in one of them.

nodes.label: Pending
nodes.detail: Waiting to be scheduled or for images to be pulled. Stuck here usually means no node fits or the image cannot be pulled.

nodes.label: Init containers
nodes.detail: Each init container must exit 0 before the next starts and before app containers start.

nodes.label: Running
nodes.detail: Containers are started. Readiness probes decide whether it receives traffic.

nodes.label: Succeeded
nodes.detail: Typical for Jobs. The Pod is not restarted.

nodes.label: Failed
nodes.detail: With restartPolicy Never. With Always or OnFailure the kubelet restarts the container instead.

nodes.label: CrashLoopBackOff
nodes.detail: The container keeps exiting, so the kubelet waits 10s, 20s, 40s... up to 5 minutes between restarts.

k8s-deployment-rollout.title: Deployment rolling update
k8s-deployment-rollout.description: A Deployment owns ReplicaSets. A rollout scales the new one up while the old one scales down.

nodes.label: Deployment
nodes.detail: You change the Pod template (for example the image). The Deployment creates a new ReplicaSet for it.

nodes.label: ReplicaSet web-7d9
nodes.detail: Kept around with 0 replicas so you can roll back.

nodes.label: ReplicaSet web-5f2
nodes.detail: Scaled up step by step, limited by maxSurge.

nodes.label: Pods v1
nodes.detail: Removed gradually, limited by maxUnavailable, so capacity never drops too far.

nodes.label: Pods v2
nodes.detail: Must pass readiness before old Pods are removed.

nodes.label: Service
nodes.detail: Sends traffic only to Ready Pods, so users see no downtime.

k8s-service-routing.title: How a Service routes traffic
k8s-service-routing.description: A Service is a stable name and IP. Its selector picks the Pods; only Ready Pods receive traffic.

nodes.label: Client Pod
nodes.detail: Uses the Service DNS name; CoreDNS resolves it to the ClusterIP.

nodes.label: CoreDNS
nodes.detail: Cluster DNS. Resolves Service names to ClusterIPs.

nodes.label: Service
nodes.detail: A virtual IP that does not belong to any one Pod. kube-proxy turns it into Pod endpoints.

nodes.label: Endpoints
nodes.detail: The list of Ready Pods whose labels match the selector. Empty list means no traffic.

nodes.label: Pod web-a
nodes.detail: Matches the selector and is Ready.

nodes.label: Pod web-b
nodes.detail: Matches the selector and is Ready.

k8s-ingress-flow.title: Ingress traffic path
k8s-ingress-flow.description: External HTTP(S) enters through one load balancer and an Ingress controller that routes by host and path.

nodes.label: Browser
nodes.detail: Sends a request with a Host header and path.

nodes.label: Load balancer
nodes.detail: Cloud or MetalLB entry point in front of the controller.

nodes.label: Ingress controller
nodes.detail: Reads Ingress rules and acts as the reverse proxy. TLS is terminated here.

nodes.label: Service web
nodes.detail: Receives requests for / .

nodes.label: Service api
nodes.detail: Receives requests for /api.

nodes.label: Pods web
nodes.detail: Backends of the web Service.

nodes.label: Pods api
nodes.detail: Backends of the api Service.

nodes.label: Ingress rules
nodes.detail: The Ingress object. It is only configuration; the controller makes it real.

k8s-storage-chain.title: Persistent storage
k8s-storage-chain.description: A Pod claims storage with a PVC. A StorageClass provisions a PV, which is backed by a real disk.

nodes.label: Pod
nodes.detail: Uses the claim by name in volumes. The data outlives the Pod.

nodes.label: PersistentVolumeClaim
nodes.detail: A namespaced request for storage. Binds to one PV.

nodes.label: PersistentVolume
nodes.detail: The actual storage resource. Created by an admin or dynamically.

nodes.label: Backing disk
nodes.detail: Where bytes really live.

nodes.label: StorageClass
nodes.detail: Describes how to create volumes on demand and the reclaim policy.

k8s-rbac-model.title: RBAC model
k8s-rbac-model.description: Who (subject) can do what (verbs) on which resources, and where (namespace or cluster).

nodes.label: Subject
nodes.detail: The identity making the request.

nodes.label: RoleBinding
nodes.detail: Grants the Role to subjects inside one namespace.

nodes.label: Role
nodes.detail: A set of allowed actions, e.g. get, list on pods.

nodes.label: Resources
nodes.detail: What the verbs apply to.

nodes.label: ClusterRoleBinding
nodes.detail: Grants a ClusterRole in every namespace. Use sparingly.

nodes.label: ClusterRole
nodes.detail: Like a Role but can also cover nodes, namespaces and non-namespaced resources.

k8s-troubleshoot-flow.title: Pod troubleshooting flow
k8s-troubleshoot-flow.description: Read the STATUS column first, then follow the matching branch.

nodes.label: kubectl get pods
nodes.detail: Start here. The status already narrows the problem.

nodes.label: Pending
nodes.detail: kubectl describe pod, then read Events: Insufficient cpu/memory, taints, unbound PVC.

nodes.label: ImagePullBackOff
nodes.detail: Check the image name and tag, the registry and imagePullSecrets.

nodes.label: CrashLoopBackOff
nodes.detail: kubectl logs --previous shows why the last run died.

nodes.label: describe + events
nodes.detail: Events list scheduling and pull failures with a clear reason.

nodes.label: logs --previous
nodes.detail: Application errors before the crash. Exit 137 means OOMKilled.

nodes.label: Fix and re-apply
nodes.detail: Change the manifest, apply, watch the rollout.

k8s-hpa-loop.title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
k8s-hpa-loop.description: Every 15 seconds the HPA compares measured usage with the target and changes the replica count.

nodes.label: metrics-server
nodes.detail: Collects resource usage from kubelets and exposes it through the metrics API.

nodes.label: HPA
nodes.detail: Computes desired = ceil(current * usage / target) within min and max.

nodes.label: Deployment
nodes.detail: The scale target. The HPA writes its replicas field.

nodes.label: Pods
nodes.detail: Utilisation is measured against CPU requests, so requests must be set.

k8s-config-injection.title: Configuration into a Pod
k8s-config-injection.description: ConfigMaps and Secrets keep settings out of the image. They reach the container as env vars or files.

nodes.label: ConfigMap
nodes.detail: Non-sensitive settings.

nodes.label: Secret
nodes.detail: Sensitive values. Base64 is encoding, not encryption.

nodes.label: Environment variables
nodes.detail: Read once at container start. Changes need a restart.

nodes.label: Mounted files
nodes.detail: Files update in place when the object changes (except subPath).

nodes.label: Container
nodes.detail: Your app sees both as ordinary env vars and files.

k8s-statefulset-identity.title: StatefulSet identity
k8s-statefulset-identity.description: Each replica keeps a stable name, a stable DNS entry and its own volume, even after a restart.

nodes.label: Headless Service
nodes.detail: Gives each Pod its own DNS record: db-0.db, db-1.db.

nodes.label: db-0
nodes.detail: Ordered startup: db-1 waits for db-0 to be Ready.

nodes.label: db-1
nodes.detail: Keeps its name when rescheduled.

nodes.label: PVC data-db-0
nodes.detail: Created from volumeClaimTemplates. Survives Pod deletion.

nodes.label: PVC data-db-1
nodes.detail: Reattached to db-1 whenever it comes back.

k8s-cronjob-flow.title: CronJob → Job → Pods
k8s-cronjob-flow.description: A CronJob creates a Job on a schedule. The Job runs Pods until the required completions succeed.

nodes.label: CronJob
nodes.detail: Creates a Job each time the schedule fires. concurrencyPolicy controls overlaps.

nodes.label: Job
nodes.detail: Tracks successful Pod completions and retries up to backoffLimit.

nodes.label: Pod
nodes.detail: Runs once. Never restarted after success.

nodes.label: History
nodes.detail: Old Jobs kept for logs, then cleaned up.

k8s-network-policy-flow.title: NetworkPolicy
k8s-network-policy-flow.description: With a default-deny policy, only traffic that a rule allows reaches the selected Pods.

nodes.label: web Pods
nodes.detail: Allowed by the rule below.

nodes.label: monitoring ns
nodes.detail: Allowed through a namespaceSelector.

nodes.label: NetworkPolicy
nodes.detail: Selects Pods and lists permitted ingress sources and ports.

nodes.label: api Pods
nodes.detail: Receive only what the policy allows.

nodes.label: other Pods
nodes.detail: Blocked. Needs a CNI that enforces policies.
